english.title: Fail to ensure silage is stored / placed / opened / removed as required by regulation 3

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Water Resources Control of Pollution Silage
Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil Wales Regulations 2010

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who had custody or control of

(A)_[silage that was being made or stored, failed to ensure that the silage was kept in a silo that satisfied the requirements of Schedule 1 to the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Wales) Regulations 2010 in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)]_
(B)_[silage that was being made or stored, failed to ensure that the silage was compressed into bales that were wrapped and sealed into impermeable membranes, or enclosed in impermeable bags and stored at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that effluent escaping from the bales could enter]_
(C)_[silage that was being made or stored, failed to ensure ,the silage being a crop being made into field silage, that the NRBW was given notice of the place where the silage was to be made or stored at least 14 days before the place was first used for that purpose and that it was at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant water abstraction point of any protected water supply source that silage could enter if it escaped]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 3(1) and 10(1) of the Water Resources (Control of Pollution) (Silage, Slurry and Agricultural Fuel Oil) (Wales) Regulations 2010.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment A fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
